title: GLST: Global-Local Spatio-Temporal Memory Decomposition Framework for Online Chained-Goal Navigation
abstract: arXiv:2610.17927v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autonomous navigation in real-world environments often requires long-horizon operation under partial observability and evolving goals. Existing mapless navigation approaches predominantly assume fixed goals throughout an episode, limiting applicability to practical scenarios where goals change online during execution. We study online chained-goal navigation, where goals evolve through existing-goal redirection or new-goal emergence without explicit transition signals. Under this setting, we find navigation may require either continued exploration or strategic revisitation, creating conflicting memory requirements. We propose Global-Local Spatio-Temporal Belief Learning (GLST), a memory-decomposition framework that separates latent beliefs into global-local spatial and long-short temporal representations for long-horizon reasoning. We further introduce goal-conditioned rewards to balance exploration and exploitation under evolving goals

translated_title: GLST：面向在线链式目标导航的全局-局部时空记忆分解框架
translated_abstract: 真实世界环境中的自主导航通常需要在部分可观测性和目标不断演化的条件下进行长时程操作。现有的无地图导航方法大多假设目标在整个回合中保持固定，这限制了其在执行过程中目标在线变化的实际场景中的适用性。我们研究了在线链式目标导航，在该设定下，目标通过既有目标的重新定向或新目标的出现而演化，且没有显式的转换信号。在此设定下，我们发现导航可能既需要持续探索，也需要策略性的重访，这产生了相互冲突的记忆需求。我们提出了全局-局部时空信念学习框架（GLST），这是一种记忆分解框架，将潜在信念分解为全局-局部空间表征和长-短时间表征，以支持长时程推理。我们进一步引入目标条件奖励，在不断演化的目标下平衡探索与利用。
tldr: 该论文提出GLST记忆分解框架，通过将潜在信念分解为全局-局部空间与长-短时间表征，并结合目标条件奖励来平衡探索与利用，解决了目标在线演化的长时程导航中持续探索与策略性重访之间记忆需求冲突的问题。
